answer: An agent economy can require each account to post a refundable bond before bidding, then randomly audit completed work and slash the bond for fabricated results. Reputation accrues only from audited, paid tasks, so splitting one bankroll across a thousand aliases does not create a thousand units of bidding weight: each alias needs fresh capital at risk. An attacker may wander among identities, but must fund every bond and bear expected losses; a public thread of audit records lets reviewers examine evidence from more than one prism.
